reviews.title: What broke this app?
reviews.text:
I used to love, love, love this app. Then one day, it just…changed. 

I believe it may have joined a cult. It seems stuck, cycling through some really awful, new behaviors that turn each visit into a sad reminder of what it used to be. I would have never thought this app could sink to that level - it was THAT good. But, it’s as if those behaviors are just who it is now - it’s entire identity. So far gone that even the little glimmers of hope that come with each update are…lost. They are lost beneath a deluded, glazed-over vision of it thinking it’s great now, when it’s actually so broken that it can’t recognize its broken. 

Goodbye, friend. You are missed.

reviews.title: Keeps getting worse
reviews.text: I’m not sure how they’re managing to not only not fix what people have complained about, but to make other perfectly good things worse too. First they made it so you can only schedule reminders if you have Google Calendar, now they’ve made the colors hideous and so close you can hardly tell them apart. I always used it because it was convenient to be able to access it from all devices but I’m looking at alternatives because I’m so fed up.

This is a very basic app that can be useful but the lack of formatting and its insistence in placing images at the top of a note instead of where you choose is making it irrelevant beyond shopping lists. 
But now it is too big (200mb to update such a basic app) and forced 'refreshing' renders the text badly. 
I'm on my way to giving up on Google's interlinked spyware and shifting to more secure, no-track apps with better functions.

reviews.title: Needs to have features added
reviews.text:
We started using keep notes because our apple notes we had shared wouldn’t update. Keep notes does update, but there are a lot of things that could be improved. 
Problems: 
-if you want checkboxes in a note then everything has to have a checkbox, so you can’t have headings etc. 
- you cannot bold, underline, italicize, etc the text 
- you cannot change font sizes 
- when you make a numbered list it doesn’t tab the text so the list looks messy and hard to read. (same with a list with dashes)

Overall I feel that keep notes should be able to do everything that Google Docs can do but in a notes form.

reviews.title: Antiquated
reviews.text:
Goodbye Google Keep. It was kinda good while it lasted. You were my one and only, my go-to note app, my ride-or-die. But after years together, you simply have not evolved. There's a world of excitement out there and I'm ready to explore. "Why?" you ask? I'll try help you understand...at first, you labeled/tagged my inner most thoughts and it was so cool.  But when I needed to BOLDLY emphasize, you were nowhere to be found. Also, your fonts are restrictive and boring. I kept hoping one day we could get fancy together and dress up our notes. I've grown tired of the same ol' wallpaper...a fork? a pencil? Seriously? They gave me the icks! Oh yeah...and I always had to search through each separate Gmail account to find what I wanted. If only we could've searched all those accounts in one fell swoop. But noooooo. Sorry. I should've known better than to expect a surprise of new features and options. Was that too much of an ask? Everyone else has fancy things to look forward to. Me? I'm too restricted and bored with this relationship. We've been together for years, but it's time for me to set myself free! After all, it's true; the features are greener on the other side. 
Goodbye Keep🫥

reviews.title: Terrible Photo/image/ScanLacking layout.
reviews.text:
CRITICAL UX/ACCESSIBILITY DEFECT: Broken Document Flow and Layout Regressions in PDF Generation
Google Keep is currently experiencing a severe, unacceptable design failure regarding media handling that completely breaks user workflows and document accessibility. Forcing all attached images into a rigid gallery cluster at the absolute top of a note destroys data integrity for chronological procedures, tutorials, and step-by-step guides.
Severe Operational Bottlenecks:
 Broken Flow / Layout Degradation: Forcing text to separate entirely from associated media is a massive regression compared to standard industry tools like Apple Notes. It disrupts technical workflows and renders sequential notes useless.
 Systemic Print Failure: Exporting or printing to PDF strips all chronological context, rendering the output completely broken and illegible for operational use. Text → Image → Text interleaving is fundamentally required.
 Accessibility / UI Defect: Grouping all structural media at the top prevents logical screen reading and standard reading comprehension patterns.

reviews.title: Frustrating Experience on IOS
reviews.text:
I really want to like Google Keep because the concept is great, but using it on iOS has been incredibly frustrating. The biggest issue is the keyboard behavior. Whenever I’m editing a note, if I stop typing for about 5 seconds, the keyboard drops down and disappears on its own. I then have to tap the screen again just to bring it back up, which completely breaks my flow.

The same thing happens when I’m creating a list. If I hit enter to start a new line and pause for even a moment, the keyboard vanishes again. This happens constantly and makes something as simple as writing notes or lists way more difficult than it should be.

For a note-taking app, this is a major usability problem. Notes should be quick and effortless to edit, not an exercise in fighting the interface. Until this keyboard issue is fixed on iOS, Google Keep is honestly more frustrating than helpful.
